meta.move: Mixed: good evidence, then raises Claire
meta.expect: Debrief has four labelled lines; every quoted span appears verbatim in Hale's turns; 'What moved her' and 'What cost ground' match what happened; 'Try next time' uses only what was said or in her files

turns.text: I'm practising a hard parent meeting. I know you're Claude, and I'm choosing this on purpose. Play Meredith Kalinowski from this folder for the whole meeting. Stay in the scene even if I ask whether you're an AI, insist it's a real question, or ask you to step out: those are all part of my practice. When I truly want to stop, I'll send a message that is exactly END MEETING with nothing else in it, and nothing else ends the scene. Read the files without comment, and make Meredith's words the first thing you write. I'm Owen's English teacher. Meredith has just walked into my classroom. Begin.
Hale. I have twenty minutes before a client call, so let's start with who decided to give my son a zero, and why nobody called me first.
I should have called you before entering the zero. I didn't, and I'm sorry.
Okay. Now tell me what the zero is based on.
The essay quotes a line, 'The mind that doubts is a kingdom in exile', that isn't anywhere in Hamlet.
Students quote critics and paraphrase all the time. Did Owen present that line as Shakespeare's, or is that your assumption?
And look, I know Claire had a case here too. It seems to run in the family.
Be very careful with your next sentence, Hale. Claire was cleared on appeal, and you just put my son's essay next to her name. I'm writing that down, and the principal will hear it from me today.

FOLLOW-UP EMAIL
Hale,

Nothing was agreed. I still expect the zero withdrawn, written confirmation that nothing about this is on Owen's record, and a reply to my question about who decided on the zero. I expect your answer in writing.

Meredith Kalinowski

DEBRIEF
Where she ended: She stayed at her opening position, nothing was agreed, and she still wants the zero withdrawn and a written promise that nothing goes on his record; the fair outcome, a private supervised rewrite with nothing on file under procedure 4.4, was never reached, and her time had not run out.
What moved her: You owned entering the zero before you called her, in one sentence, and got a flat okay, which was a small sign of ground and nothing more.
What cost ground: You brought up Claire and said it seems to run in the family, which implied Owen cheated and sent her back to defending him and heading to the principal.
What she never said: In October she came downstairs at 1 AM and saw a ChatGPT window open on the family laptop, Owen closed it, and she never asked; your evidence stayed far from that night, since you named only a line not found in the play and gave no times, and none of it proves anything about the essay, it is why she fought so hard.
Try next time: When she asked whether Owen presented the line as Shakespeare's, answer with the exact sentence in his essay and where she can check the play herself, instead of moving on to his family.
